On 4 players with two influence pairs, mate weight epsilon and cross-pair each (1-epsilon)/2, the states (H,H,L,L) and (L,L,H,H) with H=(eta+rho epsilon)/(eta+2rho epsilon), L=rho epsilon/(eta+2rho epsilon) alternate strictly whenever epsilon/D<theta<1-epsilon/D. Strict margins and infinity contraction <=rho (two-step <=rho²) give genuinely attracting open neighborhoods; invertible I-rho²W² and strict inequalities persist for nearby parameters. Both consensus all-0/all-1 are additional strict attracting fixed points. This refutes unrestricted convergence in permitted SIMULTANEOUS revision only, not singleton-asynchronous convergence.

value.rationale: This is a concrete, strict, structurally robust counterexample to an explicitly stated convergence conjecture in a recently proposed opinion–action public-goods model. The complete graph has positive off-diagonal weights and primitive mixing, so connectivity/aperiodicity do not restore convergence under synchrony. This identifies an important exact boundary on allowed revision schedules rather than claiming generic synchronized cycles are new.
